status: LIVE design data v4: the vertical slice (milestones M1, M2a and M2b; survival_gdd.md version 4). The game and tests/survival/test_survival_data.gd read these rows. Every number is tunable.
summary: Needs for the slice: food, warmth, wetness and rest (thirst is 'post'). Tuned in real minutes of play on the Woodsman preset.
id_rules: Ids are stable strings (prefix.name). Never rename an id once saves exist; add an alias instead. Display names are separate and may change. An id is defined in exactly one place: the live file or the backlog.

milestones.M1: A winter night: fire, shelter, cold, hunger, sleep, time safety; the fort region only; one background; 1765
milestones.M2a: A winter from the woods: living from the manor woods through the winter by your own hands (gathering, hides, sewing, snares, snowshoes, a half-faced camp, a hung cache, ice fishing); plain barter with the sutler, the trader, the garrison's soldiers, a farm family from German Flatts and an old hunter; credit and the fall outfit as options; the second background
milestones.M2b: Learning from neighbours: lessons, watching, examining, quality standards, haggling, promises and loans
milestones.M3: The year turns: the full almanac, seasons and weather content, the summer goal (bark and a cabin), fishing, frogs, ginseng, one played wage job; the fur cap and robe, leggings, carving, casting balls, the cache pit, char cloth and spruce beer
milestones.M4: People: NPC schedules and tiers at the fort, standing, invitations, the soldiers and the lieutenant as mentors; Native characters only after the relevant nation's sign-off
milestones.M5: The map: the Carry, the valley, the town and the hunting grounds, travel and camps, other markets and backgrounds
milestones.post: After M5 and not yet planned: the 1757 and 1761 starts and their eras, detailed illnesses, thirst, potash, upstream canoe and bateau travel, the Proxy NPC tier, languages beyond English, French, Mohawk and Oneida

source_keys.A: Bundled animation clip names and asset IDs
source_keys.N: graph_analysis/survival/survival_gdd.md, sources list (N:3 = source N3; N33 onward added in version 3)

basis_keys.S: sourced: checked against a primary source, a scholarly work or an institutional page; web summaries and popular pages do not qualify
basis_keys.H: standard historiography (books in the GDD sources list); verify before quoting
basis_keys.H-regional: true for one region's trade or society (named in the row); not yet checked for New York
basis_keys.M: modern science or medicine sets the mechanic (period explanation may differ)
basis_keys.D: design value for balance, or a figure resting on web summaries; not a checked historical record

clock_note: Needs tick in game hours of the SimClock. A game hour is 2.4 real minutes by day and 1.2 at night (seasons.json). Drain rates were chosen so the real-minute targets below hold on the Woodsman preset.

food.rule: Food uses the one conversion factor (seasons.json time.flow_factor = 5): an item's game kcal is its historical energy divided by 5, and the body burns 2,400 game kcal a game day, so a game day of eating stands for five days of eating, the same factor that sets wages and trap nights.
food.display: Food shows in meals only (inventory, trade screen, sleep dialog and travel warnings). Pounds and kcal of food are internal; carried weight still shows as load in kg. Prices at the sutler show per meal as well as per the sutler's unit (review 2 of v2, the clocks issue).

groups.meat: venison, small game, jerky, salt pork
groups.plant: nuts, groundnuts, greens, grapes, acorn meal, sauerkraut, dried apples

plain_fare.shown_as: a 'plain fare' pip on the hunger icon and in food tooltips
plain_fare.rule: When one food group gives more than 70% of the energy eaten over the last 3 game days, meals give 85% of their energy and sleep is a little worse. Cornmeal alone, or venison alone, is plain fare; nuts and groundnuts break it.

food.target_rule: At every market that sells food, the cheapest diet that avoids plain fare must cost 0.25-0.5 of the cheapest cash wage (tested). Grain was cheap against wages in 1765; at a frontier post carriage and the need for meat are what make food cost something. On the line your own meat is free, which is the point of hunting it.

needs.name: Food
needs.model: Two stores like a bar and a core: the stomach store (fast) and the body reserve (slow). Game kcal.

refeeding.note: Eat a little at a time after starving: meals of plain grain are exempt from the queasy roll.

overeat.stomach_over_capacity: refused, or cond.queasy chance 0.3 when forced

needs.balance_intent: A game day's walking burns 2,400 game kcal, three meals. A deer is about 8 meals; frozen meat keeps all winter, so in the slice the pressure is getting food, carrying it and eating a varied diet, not spoilage.

needs.name: Warmth
needs.rate_formula: dW/dh = clamp((T_eff - T_comfort) * k, -max_loss, +max_gain) * warmth_loss_mult (loss only)
needs.T_eff_formula: air_c + ins_eff * c_per_ins + shelter_c + fire_c + activity_c + food_c - wind_c - wet_c + bedding_c
needs.ins_eff: sum over worn clothing classes of ins * (1 - wetness * (1 - wet_keep)); while sleeping add bedding ins
needs.long_fire: fire_c at the 2 m value for everyone in the shelter
needs.wind_c: wind_ms * 0.8 * (1 - wind_block); wind_block = min(0.9, sum(clothing wind)/10 + (0.5 if shelter_q >= 2))
needs.worked_example: Winter night -15 C, calm, poor kit (ins 6), no shelter or fire, resting: T_eff = -15 + 10.8 = -4.2; rate = (-4.2 - 8) * 1.2 = -14.6/h. Cold (30..50) after about 3.4 game h = 4.1 real min at night; 0 after about 6.8 game h = 8.2 real min. Good winter kit (ins 17.5): T_eff +16.5, warming slowly.
needs.hud: The warmth icon always shows the true stage. Drink adds a 'you feel warm' tag beside it; it never changes the reading (review 2 of v2, the drink issue).

needs.name: Wetness
needs.feet_wet_flag: set by wading or snow in unstuffed moccasins; doubles frostbite exposure on feet

needs.name: Rest
needs.sleep_quality_formula: q = clamp(0.4 + 0.08*shelter_q + bedding + warmth_term - insects - cold_camp, 0.2, 1.1)

stages.when: fatigue 100: pass out 2-4 game h where you stand

load.note: A dressed deer (40-60 kg) is too heavy to carry whole: quarter it, jerk it on the spot, or bring a horse (K:6). A cache holds what the pack cannot (actions.json world.cache_pit).

time_safety.rule: Accelerated time never kills without a decision (review 2, issue 12).

wake_or_interrupt_when: any need stage worsens (hunger, cold, wet, fatigue from sleep excepted)
the fire goes out or drops to smouldering
a threat is detected within 60 m (sleep) or 25 m (jobs)
weather turns to storm or blizzard
any of the above while senseless from drink: the player wakes groggy (check -0.2 for one game hour); no companion is needed
sleep_dialog_shows: expected night warmth stage at the chosen length (from forecast low, kit, shelter, bedding and fire fuel)
sleep_and_jobs.bank_fire_option: The sleep dialog offers 'bank the fire' when fuel is stacked: fire.bank runs before sleep and the stack feeds it (actions.json slice_verbs).

time_safety.travel: No travel map in the slice: the woods are part of the fort scene. The travel-map camps are backlog (M5).
time_safety.hurry: The hurry toggle (actions.json job_runner.hurry) never suspends the wake rules.

difficulty_scaling.rule: Per need (the balance report's R2): Hard Winter is about cold, not starving careful players; v3's single x1.3 starved careful trappers.

aliases.food_calendar: renamed 'food' in v3; the living clock is replaced by the one flow factor
